turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The dominant effect is the process route, not composition.**
Sorting `target` reveals three clear clusters:

| Route (signature) | typical target |
|---|---|
| As-rolled / normalized only (THT=30, CT=30, DT=30, TT=30) | 225–275 MPa |
| Through-hardened + high-temperature temper (THT≈825–865, TT=550–680, TCr=8–24) | 350–650 MPa |
| **Carburized route** (NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, **CT=930 with Ct>0**, **DT≈850–896, Dt=15–70**, QmT=60–140, **TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5**) | **838–1190 MPa** |

Every one of the top ~30 samples is the carburizing route. So the recipe must set NT=930, no through-hardening step (THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0), full carburizing (CT=930, long Ct), diffusion at ~850 °C, quench-medium temp high, and a **low-temperature temper (TT≈160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5)**. High tempering temperature (550–680) is what pins the through-hardened group at 450–650 MPa.

**2. Within the carburized group:** highest values (1054–1190) have long carburizing time (Ct≈450–540), DT=850 with Dt=15 or DT≈895 with Dt=70, QmT=140 preferred slightly over 60, TT=160 ≥ 200.

**3. Composition inside the carburized group:** low base carbon (0.17–0.23, since the case is carburized), and either high Ni (1.6–1.7 with Mo 0.16–0.21) or high Cr (1.1–1.17). The single best point (1190) = C 0.23, Si 0.35, Mn 0.51, Ni 1.69, Cr 0.55, Mo 0.18, Cu 0.11, low P (0.008) and S (0.012), RedRatio 860. Runners-up (1144, 1124) share high Ni+Mo or high Cr+Mo → keep Ni high, Mo at/near max, and push Cr modestly up toward the high-Cr winners. Impurities P and S trend unfavorable, so set them low; inclusion ratings dA/dB/dC show no benefit at high values → keep small.

**4. RedRatio** shows no strong monotone trend in the top group (240–860 all appear); keep near the best-performer value (~860).

## Proposal

Carburized, low-temperature-tempered, Ni–Cr–Mo case-hardening steel with long carburizing time and clean melt chemistry:

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.22, Si=0.33, Mn=0.55, P=0.002, S=0.003, Ni=1.70, Cr=0.75, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.22, RedRatio=860, dA=0.02, dB=0.0, dC=0.0
